questions.question: Write an equation for the decomposition of solid sodium azide (NaN3) into nitrogen gas and sodium only. State symbols not required.
steps: Products are sodium (Na) and nitrogen (N2) only.
Balance nitrogen atoms: 3 N per NaN3, so N2 needs a coefficient of 3 per 2 N atoms.
Give 2 NaN3 on the left, which provides 6 N atoms, equal to 3 N2 on the right.
Balance sodium: 2 Na on the right.

questions.question: Using pV = nRT, calculate the mass of sodium azide needed to produce 120 dm3 of nitrogen at 101 000 Pa and 25 C, in the reaction 2NaN3 -> 2Na + 3N2. Give the answer to an appropriate number of significant figures.
questions.answer: About 210 g of NaN3 (212 g if 3 s.f. is used)
steps: Moles of N2 from pV = nRT: n = (101000 x 0.120) / (8.31 x 298) = 4.89 mol.
Mole ratio from 2NaN3 -> 3N2: mol NaN3 = (2/3) x 4.89 = 3.26 mol.
Mr(NaN3) = 23.0 + (3 x 14.0) = 65.0 (Ar values standard, not given in text).
120 dm3 has 2 s.f., so give about 210 g.

questions.question: Calculate the atom economy, by mass, for the production of nitrogen in reaction A of the airbag. Give the answer to an appropriate number of significant figures.
steps: Atom economy = (Mr of desired product / total Mr of all reactants) x 100; the desired product is N2.
Atom economy = 28.0 / 432.2 x 100 = 6.48%, quoted to 3 s.f. to match the Ar data.

questions.question: State the type of reaction taking place in reaction B of the airbag.
questions.answer: Combination (addition/synthesis): three reactants join to form one product
steps: Reaction B is K2O + Na2O + SiO2 -> Na2K2SiO4, so several reactants give a single product.
A reaction in which the reactants simply add together to make one product is a combination (addition, synthesis) reaction.
It can also be described as an acid-base reaction, with basic oxides K2O and Na2O reacting with acidic SiO2, but no atoms change oxidation state.

questions.question: How many atoms are there in 36.0 g of water? Avogadro constant = 6.02 x 10^23 mol-1. Options A 3.010 x 10^23, B 1.204 x 10^24, C 2.408 x 10^24, D 3.612 x 10^24.
steps: Mr(H2O) = 18.0, so moles of water = 36.0 / 18.0 = 2.00 mol.
Each H2O molecule contains 3 atoms, so moles of atoms = 3 x 2.00 = 6.00 mol.

questions.question: What is the atom economy, by mass, for the formation of iron in Fe2O3 + 3CO -> 2Fe + 3CO2? Ar: C 12.0, O 16.0, Fe 55.8. Options A 29.7%, B 45.8%, C 55.9%, D 71.7%.
steps: Atom economy = (mass of desired product / total mass of reactants) x 100.

questions.question: Complete the equation for the reaction of magnesium carbonate powder with hydrochloric acid by adding state symbols.
steps: Magnesium carbonate powder is an insoluble solid: (s).
Hydrochloric acid and magnesium chloride are in aqueous solution: (aq).
Water is a liquid: (l); carbon dioxide is a gas: (g).

questions.question: Plot a graph of the results of the five experiments on the molar volume of CO2 (mass of magnesium carbonate against volume of gas).
questions.answer: Graph of volume of gas (y-axis) against mass of MgCO3 (x-axis): five points plotted and a straight line of best fit through the origin (gradient about 250-260 cm3 g^-1)
steps: Axes: mass of magnesium carbonate / g on the x-axis (0 to 0.30, so 0.05 g per large square) and volume of gas collected / cm3 on the y-axis (0 to 80, so 10 cm3 per large square), both labelled with units.
Plot the five points accurately (to within half a small square): (0.05, 11), (0.10, 27), (0.15, 38), (0.20, 54), (0.25, 63).
Draw one straight line of best fit through the origin (0 g of MgCO3 gives 0 cm3 of gas) with points balanced about the line: 0.10 and 0.20 lie just above it; 0.05, 0.15 and 0.25 lie just below.
The gradient of this line is about 258 cm3 per g, i.e. volume is directly proportional to mass.

questions.question: Give the volume of gas collected in the further experiment using the inverted measuring cylinder.
steps: The cylinder is inverted over the water, so the scale is upside down: 0 is at the closed top end and values increase downwards.
The gas is the clear region at the top; the water level is the grey region below it, and the gas volume is read at the water surface.
Between 40 and 45 there are 5 divisions, so each division is 1 cm3.
The bottom of the meniscus is level with the first line below 45, which is 46 cm3.

questions.question: Using the graph from (b)(i), determine the mass of magnesium carbonate that gave the volume in (b)(ii).
questions.answer: About 0.18 g (accept about 0.17 to 0.19 g from a sound line of best fit)
steps: On the graph from (i), find 46 cm3 on the volume axis.
Draw a horizontal line across to the line of best fit, then a vertical line down to the mass axis.
Reading the mass axis gives about 0.18 g; as a check, 46 cm3 / 258 cm3 g^-1 = 0.178 g.
Show the construction lines on the graph.

questions.question: Calculate the molar volume of CO2 from the answers to (b)(ii) and (b)(iii). Ar: Mg 24.3, C 12.0, O 16.0.
questions.answer: About 21.5 dm3 mol^-1 (21 500 cm3 mol^-1); 22 dm3 mol^-1 to 2 s.f. (value depends on the graph reading)
steps: MgCO3 + 2HCl -> MgCl2 + H2O + CO2 gives 1 mol CO2 per 1 mol MgCO3, so n(CO2) = 2.14 x 10^-3 mol.
Molar volume = 46 cm3 / 2.14 x 10^-3 mol = 21 500 cm3 mol^-1 = 21.5 dm3 mol^-1.
Give 2 s.f. (22 dm3 mol^-1) because the volume (46) and mass (0.18) are each 2 s.f.; the unit is dm3 mol^-1.

questions.question: Find the minimum concentration of HCl needed for 30 cm3 of acid to react completely with 0.25 g of MgCO3. Ar: Mg 24.3, C 12.0, O 16.0.
steps: MgCO3 + 2HCl -> MgCl2 + H2O + CO2, so moles HCl = 2 x 2.97 x 10^-3 = 5.93 x 10^-3 mol.
Concentration = moles / volume = 5.93 x 10^-3 / 0.030 dm3 = 0.198 mol dm-3.

questions.question: Give two reasons why the molar volume of CO2 calculated in (b)(iv) was lower than expected, assuming the correct amounts of acid and magnesium carbonate were used.
questions.answer: Some CO2 dissolves in the water/acid; some CO2 escapes from the apparatus (leak or gas lost before the reading) or stays in the flask
steps: A lower molar volume means the measured gas volume was lower than expected for the moles of CO2.
Reason 1: CO2 is slightly soluble in water, so some of the gas dissolves and is not collected.
Reason 2: some gas escapes from the apparatus (a leak or gas lost before the cylinder is read).
Other valid point: some CO2 remains in the flask or delivery tube.

questions.question: A 2 kg sample of water contains 40 ppm by mass of nitrate ions. What is the mass, in g, of nitrate ions? Options A 8 x 10^-2, B 5 x 10^-5, C 8 x 10^-5, D 5 x 10^-8.
steps: 1 ppm by mass means 1 g of solute per 10^6 g of solution.
Mass of nitrate = 40 x 10^-6 x 2000 = 0.080 g = 8 x 10^-2 g.

questions.question: Propanol (3.42 g) dehydrates to propene with a yield of 85.2%. What mass of propene forms? Mr: C3H7OH 60, C3H6 42. Options A 2.04, B 2.39, C 2.91, D 4.16.
steps: Mole ratio is 1:1, so theoretical moles of propene = 0.0570 mol.
Theoretical mass of propene = 0.0570 x 42 = 2.394 g.

questions.question: What is the relative formula mass of (NH4)2Fe(SO4)2.6H2O? Options A 284, B 302, C 312, D 392.
steps: Anhydrous part: 2 NH4 = 36.0; Fe = 55.8; 2 SO4 = 2 x 96.1 = 192.2; total = 284.0.

questions.question: In 1.31 g of a titanium chloride there is 0.528 g of titanium. What is the empirical formula? Ar: Ti 47.9, Cl 35.5. Options A TiCl, B TiCl2, C TiCl3, D Ti2Cl4.
Hydrated calcium sulfate, CaSO4.xH2O, is heated to constant mass giving 3.405 g of CaSO4 and 0.900 g of water. Find x. Mr CaSO4 = 136.2. Options A 0.5, B 2, C 3, D 4.
What is the percentage atom economy, by mass, for the production of hydrogen in the reaction shown? Options A 8.8%, B 17.6%, C 21.4%, D 82.4%.
steps: Atom economy = (Mr of desired product H2 formed / total Mr of reactants) x 100.

questions.question: A compound has Mr = 84 and is 71.4% C, 9.6% H and 19.0% O by mass. What is its molecular formula? Options A C4H3O2, B C4H4O2, C C5H8O, D C6H10O.
steps: Divide by the smallest (1.19): C 5.0 : H 8.1 : O 1.0, so empirical formula = C5H8O.
Mr(C5H8O) = 60 + 8 + 16 = 84, equal to the given Mr, so molecular formula = C5H8O.

questions.question: How many molecules are there in 44.0 g of carbon monoxide? Options A 3.83 x 10^23, B 6.02 x 10^23, C 9.46 x 10^23, D 1.89 x 10^24.
Which conversion has the lowest percentage atom economy (by mass) for the formation of CaCl2? A Ca + Cl2; B Ca + 2HCl; C CaCO3 + 2HCl; D CaCO3 + 2NaCl.
steps: A: all reactant atoms go to CaCl2, so 100%.
B: CaCl2 = 111.1 out of reactants 40.1 + 73.0 = 113.1, about 98%.
D: CaCl2 = 111.1 out of 100.1 + 116.9 = 217.0, about 51%, which is the lowest.

questions.question: 100 cm3 of propane is burned with 600 cm3 of oxygen: C3H8 + 5O2 -> 3CO2 + 4H2O(l). What is the total gas volume at the end (r.t.p.)? Options A 300, B 400, C 700, D 800.
steps: Oxygen needed = 5 x 100 = 500 cm3, so 100 cm3 O2 is left over (excess).
Products: 3 x 100 = 300 cm3 CO2 gas; the water is liquid, so it contributes no gas volume.
Gas left = 100 cm3 O2 + 300 cm3 CO2 = 400 cm3.

questions.question: There are 6.02 x 10^23 atoms in 0.25 mol of which substance? Options A He, B H2O, C BH3, D CH4.
steps: 1.00 mol atoms / 0.25 mol = 4 atoms per formula unit.
BH3 has 4 atoms (1 B + 3 H). He has 1, H2O has 3, CH4 has 5.

questions.question: What is the relative formula mass of Na2CO3.10H2O? Ar: H 1.0, C 12.0, O 16.0, Na 23.0. Options A 106, B 142, C 263, D 286.
Which aqueous solution contains the greatest number of ions? A 200 cm3 of 1.5 mol dm-3 MgCl2; B 400 cm3 of 0.8 mol dm-3 MgSO4; C 500 cm3 of 1.0 mol dm-3 NaCl; D 1000 cm3 of 0.25 mol dm-3 Na2SO4.
steps: Moles of formula units = concentration x volume (dm3).
A: 0.300 mol MgCl2 x 3 ions = 0.90 mol ions.
B: 0.320 mol MgSO4 x 2 ions = 0.64 mol ions.
C: 0.500 mol NaCl x 2 ions = 1.00 mol ions.
D: 0.250 mol Na2SO4 x 3 ions = 0.75 mol ions, so C is largest.

questions.question: A 1 kg seawater sample contains 6 x 10^-9 g of gold. How many gold atoms are in 1 g of this seawater, to one significant figure? Ar Au 197; L = 6 x 10^23 mol-1. Options A 2 x 10^10, B 4 x 10^12, C 2 x 10^13, D 4 x 10^15.
steps: 1 g of seawater is 1/1000 of 1 kg, so it contains 6 x 10^-12 g of gold.

questions.question: The maximum permitted sulfur concentration in diesel is 10 mg of sulfur in 1 kg of diesel. What is this in ppm? Options A 0.00001, B 0.01, C 10, D 10 000.
steps: 1 ppm by mass = 1 mg per kg.
10 mg in 1 kg = 10 mg per kg = 10 ppm.

questions.question: 3.2 kg of this diesel (10 mg S per kg) is burned in air. What is the maximum volume of SO2 at r.t.p. (molar volume 24 dm3 mol-1)? Options A 0.024, B 0.77, C 2.4, D 24.
steps: Mass of sulfur = 3.2 kg x 10 mg/kg = 32 mg = 0.032 g.
Moles S = 0.032 / 32.1 = 1.0 x 10^-3 mol, and S + O2 -> SO2 gives 1 mol SO2 per mol S.
Volume = 1.0 x 10^-3 mol x 24 dm3 mol-1 = 0.024 dm3.

questions.question: 0.23 g of sodium is added to 350 cm3 of water forming NaOH(aq) and hydrogen. What is the concentration of NaOH in mol dm-3? Options A 0.010, B 0.029, C 0.29, D 0.66.
steps: Na + H2O -> NaOH + 1/2 H2, so moles NaOH = 0.0100 mol.

questions.question: What is the maximum volume, in cm3, of hydrogen formed when 0.23 g of sodium reacts with water at r.t.p.? Options A 120, B 240, C 480, D 2800.
steps: Mole ratio Na : 1/2 H2 = 2 : 1, so moles H2 = 0.0050 mol.

questions.question: The sodium hydroxide solution was neutralised with sulfuric acid. Which is the ionic equation for this reaction?
steps: The full reaction is H2SO4 + 2NaOH -> Na2SO4 + 2H2O, a neutralisation.
Na+ and SO4 2- appear unchanged on both sides, so they are spectator ions and cancel.
What is left is H+(aq) + OH-(aq) -> H2O(l); options B, C and D either do not show this or still include spectator ions.

questions.question: For 2NaOH(aq) + MgSO4(aq) -> Mg(OH)2(s) + Na2SO4(aq), what is the atom economy (by mass) for Mg(OH)2? Ar: H 1.0, O 16.0, Na 23.0, Mg 24.3, S 32.1. Options A 29.1%, B 41.0%, C 48.4%, D 50.0%.
Which aqueous solution has the highest concentration, in mol dm-3, of chloride ions? A 0.1 g dm-3 HCl; B 0.1 g dm-3 NaCl; C 0.1 g dm-3 KCl; D 0.1 g dm-3 BaCl2.
steps: Same mass per volume in each, so the solution with the smallest molar mass per Cl- ion has the most moles of Cl-.
Per mole of Cl-: HCl 36.5 g, NaCl 58.5 g, KCl 74.6 g, BaCl2 208.2 g / 2 = 104.1 g.
HCl gives the most moles of Cl- per dm3, so A is highest.

questions.question: An oxide of lead contains 90.7% lead by mass. What is its formula? Ar: O 16.0, Pb 207.2. Options A PbO, B PbO2, C Pb2O3, D Pb3O4.
steps: Per 100 g: moles Pb = 90.7 / 207.2 = 0.438 mol; mass O = 9.3 g, moles O = 9.3 / 16.0 = 0.581 mol.

questions.question: Which gas occupies 6.0 dm3 at r.t.p. (molar volume 24.0 dm3 mol-1)? A 2.0 g He; B 4.0 g O2; C 11.0 g CO2; D 14.0 g N2.

Ten test tubes each hold 1.0 cm3 of a chromium chloride solution of concentration 0.1 mol dm-3. Different volumes of 0.1 mol dm-3 AgNO3 give AgCl precipitate; heights are plotted on a graph. What is the formula of the chromium chloride? Options A CrCl, B Cr3Cl4, C Cr4Cl3, D CrCl3.
steps: Precipitate height rises steadily then levels off at 4.0 mm once 3.0 cm3 of AgNO3 has been added, so all the Cl- has reacted at 3.0 cm3.
n(Ag+) = 0.0030 dm3 x 0.1 mol dm^-3 = 3.0 x 10^-4 mol, equal to n(Cl-) by Ag+ + Cl- -> AgCl.
n(chromium chloride) in 1.0 cm3 of 0.1 mol dm^-3 = 1.0 x 10^-4 mol.
Cl- : compound = 3.0 x 10^-4 : 1.0 x 10^-4 = 3 : 1, so the formula is CrCl3.

questions.question: Which solution contains the greatest number of ions? A 20.0 cm3 of 0.5 mol dm-3 KCl; B 0.40 dm3 of 0.03 mol dm-3 KCl; C 10.0 cm3 of 0.6 mol dm-3 CaCl2; D 0.15 dm3 of 0.04 mol dm-3 CaCl2.
steps: A: 0.0100 mol KCl x 2 = 0.020 mol ions.
B: 0.40 x 0.03 = 0.0120 mol KCl x 2 = 0.024 mol ions.
C: 0.0060 mol CaCl2 x 3 = 0.018 mol ions.
D: 0.15 x 0.04 = 0.0060 mol CaCl2 x 3 = 0.018 mol ions, so B is largest.

questions.question: Initial mass of iron powder is 6.17 g and final mass is 3.38 g. Calculate the moles of iron that reacted.
Calculate the moles of iron(III) chloride that react, given 200 cm3 of 0.500 mol dm-3 FeCl3 is used and all of it reacts.
steps: Moles FeCl3 = 0.500 mol dm-3 x 0.200 dm3 = 0.100 mol.
The solution ends containing only FeCl2, so all the FeCl3 has reacted (consistent with a 1:2 ratio to Fe).

questions.question: Use the answers to (a)(i) and (a)(ii) to write the ionic equation for the reaction of iron with iron(III) chloride, with state symbols. Show working.
steps: Moles Fe reacted : moles Fe3+ reacted = 0.0500 : 0.100 = 1 : 2.
Fe is oxidised to Fe2+ and Fe3+ is reduced to Fe2+.
Check charge: left +6, right +6; atoms balance.

questions.question: Hydrated iron(II) chloride, FeCl2.xH2O, contains 28.1% iron by mass. Calculate x. Ar: Fe 55.8, Cl 35.5, H 1.0, O 16.0.
A sample of nitrogen gas contains 1.204 x 10^22 molecules. What is its mass? Ar N 14.0; L = 6.02 x 10^23 mol-1. Options A 0.14 g, B 0.28 g, C 0.56 g, D 1.12 g.
The concentration of nitrogen dioxide in air is 0.5 ppm. What is the percentage of NO2 molecules in the air? Options A 0.5%, B 0.005%, C 0.00005%, D 0.0000005%.
steps: 1 ppm = 1 part in 10^6, so 0.5 ppm = 0.5 / 10^6 of the molecules.

questions.question: Complete the table of results for the heating of hydrated magnesium sulfate in a crucible.
questions.answer: Mass of MgSO4 after heating = 2.91 g; mass of water lost = 2.59 g
steps: Mass of magnesium sulfate after heating = 24.12 - 21.21 = 2.91 g.
Mass of water lost = mass before heating - mass after = 26.71 - 24.12 = 2.59 g.

questions.question: Use the experimental results to calculate x in MgSO4.xH2O to the nearest whole number. Ar: H 1.0, O 16.0, Mg 24.3, S 32.1.
steps: Ratio H2O : MgSO4 = 0.144 / 0.0242 = 5.95, which rounds to 6, so x = 6.

questions.question: The correct x is greater than the value calculated in (a)(ii). Suggest, using the same apparatus, a way to improve the method, and justify it.
questions.answer: Heat, cool and reweigh repeatedly until a constant mass is reached, so all the water of crystallisation is driven off
steps: A result that is too low for x means too little water was lost, so the heating was incomplete.
Two minutes of heating is not enough to drive off all the water.
Heat, cool and reweigh repeatedly until two successive masses agree (constant mass).
Constant mass shows all the water has been removed, so the mass loss is complete.

questions.question: What is the atom economy (by mass) for the formation of oxygen in 2KClO3 -> 2KCl + 3O2? Ar: O 16.0, Cl 35.5, K 39.1. Options A 13.1%, B 26.1%, C 39.2%, D 64.3%.
2 x 10^-3 mol of hexane undergoes complete combustion: C6H14 + 9.5O2 -> 6CO2 + 7H2O. How many molecules of CO2 form? Options A 1.20 x 10^21, B 7.22 x 10^21, C 8.43 x 10^21, D 3.18 x 10^23.
steps: Moles CO2 = 6 x 2 x 10^-3 = 1.2 x 10^-2 mol.

questions.question: Iron(III) oxide is reduced by hydrogen in two steps. What is the maximum mass of iron from 39.9 tonnes of Fe2O3? Ar: H 1.0, O 16.0, Fe 55.8. Options A 6.98 t, B 13.95 t, C 27.90 t, D 41.85 t.
steps: Overall, each Fe2O3 gives 2 Fe atoms, as in the final step 3Fe from Fe3O4 that came from 2Fe2O3.

questions.question: 4.08 g of CuSO4.5H2O is dissolved to make 250 cm3 of solution. What is the concentration of CuSO4 in mol dm-3? Options A 0.0163, B 0.0256, C 0.0654, D 0.102.
How many moles of copper atoms are in the piece of copper shown? Density of copper = 8.96 g cm-3. Options A 0.675, B 1.48, C 6.05, D 54.2.
steps: Mass = density x volume = 8.96 x 384 = 3440 g.
Moles = 3440 / 63.5 (Ar Cu) = 54.2 mol, which is option D.

questions.question: 2.50 g of NaCl reacts with excess Pb(NO3)2 to form PbCl2 with a 95% yield. What mass of PbCl2 forms? Mr NaCl 58.5, PbCl2 278.2. Options A 5.65 g, B 5.94 g, C 11.3 g, D 11.9 g.
steps: 2NaCl gives 1 PbCl2, so theoretical moles PbCl2 = 0.0214 mol.

questions.question: 10.0 g of NaCl is dissolved and made up to 250.0 cm3. What is the concentration in mol dm-3? Mr NaCl 58.5. Options A 0.171, B 0.684, C 10.0, D 40.0.
0.15 mol of aluminium is added to 120 cm3 of 1.50 mol dm-3 HCl: 2Al + 6HCl -> 2AlCl3 + 3H2. How much reactant is unused? Options A 0.06 mol Al, B 0.09 mol Al, C 0.03 mol HCl, D 0.13 mol HCl.
steps: Al needed to react with 0.180 mol HCl = 0.180 x 2/6 = 0.060 mol Al, so HCl is limiting.

questions.question: Which solution contains chloride ions at a concentration of 0.0500 mol dm-3? Ar: Ca 40.1, Cl 35.5, Na 23.0.
questions.answer: B: calcium chloride, 1.39 g in 500 cm3
steps: The others do not fit: A has [Cl-] = 0.100, C has [Cl-] = 1.46 / 58.5 / 0.250 = 0.100, and D has [Cl-] = 0.0250 mol dm^-3.

questions.question: 1 kg of seawater contains 64 mg of bromide ions. What is the bromide concentration in ppm by mass? Options A 0.80, B 64, C 800, D 64 000.
steps: 1 ppm by mass = 1 mg per kg.

questions.question: How many bromide ions are in 500 g of this seawater (64 mg Br- per kg)? Ar Br 80; L = 6.0 x 10^23 mol-1. Options A 2.4 x 10^20, B 4.8 x 10^20, C 1.9 x 10^22, D 3.8 x 10^22.
steps: Mass of bromide in 500 g = 64 mg/kg x 0.500 kg = 32 mg = 0.032 g.

questions.question: A gaseous mixture contains 2.19% carbon dioxide by mass. What is this in ppm by mass? Options A 2.19 x 10^6, B 2.19 x 10^4, C 2.19 x 10^-4, D 2.19 x 10^-6.

A lead nitrate solution has a concentration of 15 ppm by mass. What is the mass of lead nitrate in 400 g of this solution? Options A 6.00 x 10^-3 g, B 6.00 x 10^-6 g, C 6.00 x 10^-3 kg, D 6.00 x 10^0 kg.
steps: 15 ppm = 15 g of solute per 10^6 g of solution.
Mass of solute = 15 x 400 / 10^6 = 6.00 x 10^-3 g.

questions.question: What is the concentration of hydroxide ions in a solution containing 5.00 g of Ba(OH)2 in 250 cm3? Mr Ba(OH)2 = 171.3. Options A 0.0292, B 0.0584, C 0.1168, D 0.2335 mol dm-3.
steps: Each formula unit gives 2 OH-, so moles OH- = 0.0584 mol.

questions.question: An organic compound contains 24.2% C, 4.00% H and 71.8% Cl by mass. What is its empirical formula? Ar: H 1.0, C 12.0, Cl 35.5. Options A CHCl, B CH2Cl, C C2H4Cl2, D C4H4Cl4.
steps: Divide by 2.02: C 1 : H 1.98 : Cl 1.00, which is 1 : 2 : 1.

questions.question: The formula of calcium carbide is CaC2. What is the formula of the carbide ion?
steps: CaC2 contains Ca2+ ions, so the carbide part has charge 2-.
The carbide ion is a pair of carbon atoms bonded together with an overall 2- charge: C2^2-.

questions.question: Excess CaC2 reacts with 10 g of water to form ethyne (CaC2 + 2H2O -> C2H2 + Ca(OH)2), assuming 100% yield. What mass of ethyne forms? Mr H2O 18.0, C2H2 26.0. Options A 7.22 g, B 14.4 g, C 23.4 g, D 28.9 g.
steps: Moles H2O = 10 / 18.0 = 0.556 mol; water is the limiting reactant because CaC2 is in excess.
Mole ratio H2O : C2H2 = 2 : 1, so moles C2H2 = 0.278 mol.

questions.question: Which compound contains 2.35 x 10^22 molecules in 2.50 g? Mr: CO 28.0, CO2 44.0, SO2 64.1, SO3 80.1. Options A CO, B CO2, C SO2, D SO3.
15.0 g of vanadium reacts completely with 7.07 g of oxygen. What is the formula of the oxide? Ar: V 50.9, O 16.0. Options A VO, B V2O3, C VO2, D V2O5.
What is the pressure of 5.00 mol of nitrogen in 1.50 m3 heated to 500 K? R = 8.31 J K-1 mol-1. Options A 13.9 Pa, B 6 290 Pa, C 13 900 Pa, D 31 200 Pa.
steps: Rearrange pV = nRT to p = nRT / V.
p = 13 850 Pa, which is 13 900 Pa to 3 s.f.

questions.question: The formula of phosgene is COCl2. What is the total number of atoms in 9.9 g? Mr COCl2 = 99.0; L = 6.02 x 10^23 mol-1. Options A 1.51 x 10^22, B 6.02 x 10^22, C 1.81 x 10^23, D 2.41 x 10^23.
steps: Each molecule has 4 atoms (C, O, Cl, Cl).

questions.question: Which pair of substances contains the same number of moles at r.t.p.? Ar Ca 40, Li 7, Al 27, Mg 24; molar volume 24 dm3 mol-1. Options A 24 dm3 Cl2 and 20 g Ca; B 24 dm3 O2 and 14 g Li; C 1.2 dm3 H2 and 2.7 g Al; D 1.2 dm3 N2 and 1.2 g Mg.
steps: Moles of a gas = volume / 24 dm3 mol-1.
The other pairs give different moles (A 1 and 0.5; B 1 and 2; C 0.05 and 0.1).

questions.question: A sample of a hydrocarbon of mass 7.2 g contains 6.0 g of carbon. What is its empirical formula? Options A CH2, B C5H12, C C6H6, D C7H6.
steps: Ratio C : H = 0.50 : 1.2 = 5 : 12, so the formula is C5H12.

questions.question: There is 0.045 g of solute in 1500 g of solution. What is the concentration in ppm? Options A 3.00, B 6.75, C 30.0, D 67.5.
steps: ppm = (mass of solute / mass of solution) x 10^6.

questions.question: What is the concentration, in mol dm-3, of a solution of 7.84 g of H3PO4 in 400 cm3? Options A 0.02, B 0.08, C 0.20, D 19.6.
What volume of gas (r.t.p.) is produced by complete decomposition of 0.050 mol Ca(NO3)2 in 2Ca(NO3)2 -> 2CaO + 4NO2 + O2? Options A 600 cm3, B 1.20 dm3, C 3.00 dm3, D 6.00 dm3.
steps: 2 mol Ca(NO3)2 gives 4 NO2 + 1 O2 = 5 mol gas.

questions.question: Which is the strongest oxidising agent in Cl2 + 2Br- -> Br2 + 2Cl- and Br2 + 2I- -> 2Br- + I2? Options A chlorine, B bromide ions, C bromine, D iodide ions.
steps: Cl2 displaces Br2 from bromide, so Cl2 is a stronger oxidising agent than Br2.
Br2 displaces I2 from iodide, so Br2 is stronger than I2.
Oxidising strength falls down Group 7: Cl2 > Br2 > I2.

questions.question: Which is the simplest ionic equation for an alkali reacting with an acid? Options A 2H+ + 2OH- -> 2H2O(l), B H+ + OH- -> H2O(aq), C H+ + OH- -> H2O(l), D 2H+ + O2- -> H2O(l).
steps: Only the ions that react are shown; spectator ions are left out.
The simplest equation has one H+ and one OH- giving one H2O.
Water is a liquid, so option C with (l) is correct; A is not simplest, B wrongly gives aqueous water, D uses an oxide ion.

questions.question: What is the maximum volume of butane that can be completely burned in 39 cm3 of oxygen at r.t.p.? C4H10 + 6.5O2 -> 4CO2 + 5H2O(l). Options A 6.0 cm3, B 12 cm3, C 24 cm3, D 45 cm3.
steps: Mole ratio C4H10 : O2 = 1 : 6.5 (equal volumes at r.t.p.).

questions.question: 10 g of copper is added to excess AgNO3 solution: Cu + 2AgNO3 -> 2Ag + Cu(NO3)2. What is the mass of silver collected, assuming 100% yield? Options A between 10 g and 20 g, B 20 g, C between 20 g and 40 g, D more than 40 g.
questions.answer: C (between 20 g and 40 g, about 34 g)
steps: Mass Ag = 0.315 x 107.9 = 34.0 g, which is between 20 g and 40 g (Ar Ag is a standard value).

questions.question: What is the atom economy, by mass, for the formation of ethanol in C6H12O6 -> 2C2H5OH + 2CO2? Options A 26%, B 49%, C 51%, D 96%.
Plot a graph of the results for NaOH.xH2O heating: plot the points, label the axes and draw a line of best fit.
questions.answer: Graph of mass of NaOH (y) against mass of NaOH.xH2O (x): six points plotted, both axes labelled with units, and a straight line of best fit through the origin (gradient 0.69)
steps: Label the x-axis "Mass of NaOH.xH2O / g" and the y-axis "Mass of NaOH / g" (the grid is already numbered 0 to 8, 1 g per large square).
Draw one straight line of best fit through the origin; the points lie almost exactly on it, with gradient about 0.69.

questions.question: Use the graph to find the mass of NaOH.xH2O needed to produce 4.0 g of NaOH.
steps: On the y-axis find 4.0 g of NaOH and draw a horizontal line to the line of best fit.
Draw a vertical line down to the x-axis and read the mass of hydrate: about 5.8 g.
Check: 4.0 / 0.69 = 5.8 g. The construction lines must be shown on the graph.

questions.question: Using the answer to (a)(ii) and the equation NaOH.xH2O -> NaOH + xH2O, calculate x.
steps: Mass of water in 5.8 g of hydrate = 5.8 - 4.0 = 1.8 g, which is 1.8 / 18.0 = 0.10 mol.
From NaOH.xH2O -> NaOH + xH2O, x = n(H2O) / n(NaOH) = 0.10 / 0.100 = 1.

questions.question: Calculate the mass of NaOH.7H2O needed to make 250 cm3 of 0.150 mol dm-3 NaOH solution. Ar: Na 23.0, O 16.0, H 1.0.
Which pair of compounds will not react to form a precipitate? A AgNO3 and CaCl2; B Ca(OH)2 and CO2; C Ba(OH)2 and HCl; D KI and Pb(NO3)2.
steps: A: AgCl is insoluble, so a precipitate forms.
B: CaCO3 is insoluble and forms a precipitate.
C: BaCl2 is soluble, so no precipitate forms; it is just neutralisation.

questions.question: What is observed when iron(II) carbonate reacts with ethanoic acid? Options A colourless solution, B colourless solution and effervescence, C green solution and effervescence, D green solution.
steps: Carbonates react with acids to release CO2, seen as effervescence (fizzing).
Iron(II) salts form a pale green solution (Fe2+ ions).

questions.question: Balance xP2H4 + yO2 -> P4O10 + zH2O. Options A x=1 y=6 z=2, B x=2 y=6 z=2, C x=2 y=7 z=4, D x=4 y=9 z=8.
How many oxygen atoms are in 0.0100 mol of H2SO4? L = 6.020 x 10^23 mol-1. Options A 6.020 x 10^21, B 1.204 x 10^22, C 2.408 x 10^22, D 4.214 x 10^22.
steps: O atoms = 0.0100 x 4 = 0.0400 mol of O atoms.

questions.question: Which oxide of nitrogen contains 30% nitrogen by mass? Ar N 14.0, O 16.0. Options A NO, B NO2, C N2O, D N2O3.
The concentration of sulfur dioxide in polluted air is 0.4 ppm. What is the percentage of SO2 molecules? Options A 0.4%, B 0.004%, C 0.00004%, D 0.0000004%.
Seaweed contains 30.0 mg of iodine per kg. How many iodine atoms are in 10 kg? Ar I 126.9; L = 6.02 x 10^23 mol-1. Options A 7.12 x 10^19, B 1.42 x 10^20, C 7.12 x 10^20, D 1.42 x 10^21.
steps: Mass of iodine = 30.0 mg/kg x 10 kg = 300 mg = 0.300 g.

questions.question: An excess of Na2SO4 is added to 50 cm3 of 0.100 mol dm-3 BaCl2. What mass of BaSO4 forms? Mr BaSO4 = 233.4. Options A 1.167 g, B 2.334 g, C 11.67 g, D 23.34 g.
steps: BaCl2 + Na2SO4 gives 1 BaSO4 per BaCl2, so moles BaSO4 = 0.00500 mol.

questions.question: Flask A contains 4.0 x 10^-3 mol of methane. Flask B has 160 mg of a different gas at the same temperature and pressure, with the same number of moles. Which gas could be in flask B? Options A argon, B carbon dioxide, C helium, D neon.
steps: Same T and p and same volume means same moles.
Moles in B = moles in A = 4.0 x 10^-3 mol.
Molar mass = 0.160 g / 0.0040 mol = 40 g mol-1, which matches argon (Ar 40.0).

questions.question: Magnesium azide is an ionic compound containing N3- ions. What is its empirical formula? Options A Mg3N, B MgN2, C MgN3, D MgN6.
steps: Mg forms Mg2+, and each azide ion is N3-, so the formula is Mg(N3)2.

questions.question: The density of an unknown gas is 0.656 g dm-3 at 20 C and 101 000 Pa. Calculate its molar mass. R = 8.31 J K-1 mol-1.
steps: Use M = density x RT / p, since density = mass / volume = M x p / (RT).

questions.question: The unknown gas is a hydrocarbon. Using the molar mass from (a), give its name or formula.
steps: Molar mass from (a) is about 16 g mol-1.
Mr(CH4) = 12.0 + 4 x 1.0 = 16.0, the only hydrocarbon that matches.

questions.question: What mass of Na2CO3 is needed to make 250 cm3 of 0.100 mol dm-3 solution? Ar C 12.0, O 16.0, Na 23.0. Options A 1.30 g, B 2.65 g, C 5.30 g, D 10.6 g.
A lead block 10 cm x 10 cm x 10 cm contains 3.295 x 10^25 atoms. Calculate its density. Ar Pb 207.2; L = 6.02 x 10^23 mol-1. Options A 3.79, B 4.49, C 11.34, D 54.73 g cm-3.
Baking powder releases a gas in two types of reaction during cooking, one being neutralisation. Give the name of the second type.
questions.answer: Thermal decomposition (of sodium hydrogencarbonate on heating)
steps: Sodium hydrogencarbonate also decomposes on heating: 2NaHCO3 -> Na2CO3 + H2O + CO2.
This releases CO2 without any acid, so it is the second reaction type.

questions.question: Suggest why neutralisation does not occur in an unopened container of baking powder.
questions.answer: The acid and sodium hydrogencarbonate are dry solids and cannot dissolve or mix to react without water (moisture).
steps: Neutralisation needs the acid and the hydrogencarbonate to be in contact in solution, to form ions.
In a sealed dry container there is no water, so the solid reactants cannot mix or react.
Reaction happens only when water is added during cooking.

questions.question: The acidic derivative of tartaric acid contains 20.8% K, 25.5% C, 2.66% H, with the rest O. Calculate its empirical formula. Ar: K 39.1, C 12.0, H 1.0, O 16.0.
The acidic derivative is represented as H+K+A2-. Write the equation for its neutralisation of sodium hydrogencarbonate (state symbols not required).
steps: H+ is the acidic proton, and HCO3- reacts with it to give H2O and CO2.
The other ions K+ and A2- remain as the salt with Na+ (NaKA).
Check: H = 2 on each side, Na = 1, K = 1, C = 1 and the rest balances.

questions.question: Calculate the maximum volume, in cm3, of CO2 released from 5.00 g of baking powder (30% NaHCO3 by mass) in an oven at 190 C and 101 000 Pa, using pV = nRT.
steps: Moles NaHCO3 = 1.50 / 84.0 = 0.0179 mol, and 1 mol CO2 forms per mol NaHCO3 (from b(ii)).

questions.question: Calculate the decrease in volume when the CO2 from (b)(iii) is cooled from 190 C to 20 C at constant pressure.
questions.answer: About 250 cm3 decrease (680 cm3 to about 430 cm3)
steps: Assume constant pressure, so V is proportional to T (Kelvin).

questions.question: How many atoms are there in 10 g of methane? Ar H 1.0, C 12.0; L = 6.02 x 10^23 mol-1. Options A 3.76 x 10^23, B 9.63 x 10^23, C 1.88 x 10^24, D 4.82 x 10^24.
steps: Each CH4 has 5 atoms, so 0.625 x 5 = 3.125 mol of atoms.

questions.question: A solution contains 95 ppm of a solute. What mass of solute is dissolved in 1 kg of this solution? Options A 95 g, B 0.95 g, C 0.095 g, D 0.000095 g.
steps: 95 ppm = 95 mg per kg of solution.

questions.question: What is the total number of atoms in 8.8 g of carbon dioxide? Mr CO2 = 44; L = 6.02 x 10^23 mol-1. Options A 1.2 x 10^23, B 3.6 x 10^23, C 1.2 x 10^24, D 3.6 x 10^24.
steps: Each CO2 has 3 atoms, so 0.20 x 3 = 0.60 mol of atoms.

questions.question: How many moles of ions are in 40 cm3 of 0.050 mol dm-3 Mg(NO3)2? Options A 0.0020, B 0.0040, C 0.0060, D 0.0080 mol.
steps: Each formula unit gives 1 Mg2+ and 2 NO3-, so 3 ions.

questions.question: Three of four solutions contain the same number of moles of Cl-. Which contains a different number? A 15.0 cm3 of 0.80 mol dm-3 HCl; B 10.0 cm3 of 0.40 mol dm-3 FeCl3; C 10.0 cm3 of 0.90 mol dm-3 MgCl2; D 20.0 cm3 of 0.60 mol dm-3 NaCl.
questions.answer: C (0.018 mol Cl-, the others are 0.012 mol)
steps: D: 0.020 x 0.60 = 0.012 mol Cl-, so C is the odd one out.

questions.question: NxO4 is an oxide of nitrogen with 69.57% oxygen by mass. What is its relative molecular mass? Options A 78, B 92, C 106, D 109.
steps: Mass of O in the molecule = 4 x 16.0 = 64.0.
This gives N2O4 (N = 14 each), consistent with the formula.

questions.question: What is the atom economy, by mass, for the production of ethanoic acid in 2C4H10 + 5O2 -> 4CH3COOH + 2H2O? Options A 13%, B 67%, C 77%, D 87%.

A water molecule (H-1 and O-16) has mass 2.9908 x 10^-23 g. What is the mass of 1 amu in grams? Ar: O-16 15.995 amu, H-1 1.0080 amu. Options A 6.0185 x 10^23, B 6.0221 x 10^23, C 1.6605 x 10^-24, D 1.6616 x 10^-24.
steps: Mass of H2O in amu = 2 x 1.0080 + 15.995 = 18.011 amu.

questions.question: How many molecules of H2O are in 1 drop (0.050 cm3) of water? Density 1 g cm-3; L = 6.02 x 10^23 mol-1. Options A 2.17 x 10^26, B 6.69 x 10^23, C 1.67 x 10^22, D 1.67 x 10^21.
steps: Mass of water = 0.050 cm3 x 1 g cm-3 = 0.050 g.

questions.question: What is the maximum volume of butane that will completely burn in 130 cm3 of oxygen? C4H10 + 6.5O2 -> 4CO2 + 5H2O. Options A 10 cm3, B 15 cm3, C 20 cm3, D 40 cm3.
steps: Mole ratio C4H10 : O2 = 1 : 6.5, and gas volumes are in the same ratio.

questions.question: Which mass of fertiliser contains 467 g of nitrogen? A 2 kg NaNO3 (Mr 85); B 1 kg urea NH2CONH2 (Mr 60); C 1 kg NH4NO3 (Mr 80); D 1 kg (NH4)2SO4 (Mr 132.1).
steps: Urea NH2CONH2 has 2 N atoms, so N mass = 2 x 14 = 28 per 60 g.
A gives 2000 / 85 x 14 = 329 g; C gives 350 g; D gives 212 g.

questions.question: A sample of hydrated magnesium sulfate contains 43% water by mass. What is its formula? The answer options are not included in the extracted text.
steps: In 100 g of the hydrate there are 43 g of water and 57 g of MgSO4.
Moles of H2O = 43 / 18.0 = 2.39 mol; moles of MgSO4 = 57 / 120.4 = 0.473 mol.
Ratio H2O : MgSO4 = 2.39 / 0.473 = 5.05, which is about 5, so the formula is MgSO4.5H2O (option B).

questions.question: What volume of SO2 reacts completely with 50 cm3 of sodium hydroxide solution of concentration 0.12 mol dm-3? SO2 + 2NaOH -> Na2SO3 + H2O; molar volume 24 dm3 at room temperature and pressure. Options A 0.072 dm3, B 0.144 dm3, C 0.288 dm3, D 72 dm3.
steps: Mole ratio SO2 : NaOH = 1 : 2, so moles SO2 = 0.0030 mol.

questions.question: A 3.50 g organic compound burns forming 5.15 g of CO2 and 2.11 g of H2O. What is its empirical formula? Options A CH2O, B CH3O, C C2HO, D CH2O2.
steps: Mass C = 5.15 x 12/44 = 1.40 g; moles C = 0.117 mol.
Mass H = 2.11 x 2/18 = 0.234 g; moles H = 0.234 mol.
Ratio C : H : O = 1 : 2 : 1, so CH2O.

questions.question: Which reaction to produce copper(II) nitrate (Mr = 187.5) has an atom economy of 46.5% by mass? The answer options are not included in the extracted text.
steps: Atom economy = 187.5 / total Mr of reactants x 100.

questions.question: Which method for the preparation of hydrogen has the highest atom economy by mass? The answer options are not included in the extracted text.
steps: Atom economy for H2 = (mass of H2 made / total Mr of reactants) x 100.
B has the highest atom economy.

questions.question: Which amount does not have a mass of approximately 6 g? A 0.33 mol H2O (Mr 18); B 0.25 mol Mg (Ar 24.3); C 0.033 mol glucose (Mr 180); D 0.025 mol CuSO4 (Mr 159.6).
steps: D: 0.025 x 159.6 = 4.0 g, which is not about 6 g.
